summary: Comprehensive E2E test of AKKI Sandbox v3.0 (M0/M1/M2/M3/M5). Backend: 54/55 pytest passed (98%). Frontend: full signup→workspace→highlights→ask flow verified with real Claude LLM generating 3 signals and grounded answer with source citations. One real security bug found: brute-force lockout after 5 failed login attempts does NOT trigger (all 6+ attempts return 401 instead of 429).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout broken: after 5 failed attempts the 6th+ still returns 401 (not 429). Verified via direct curl loop — 6 identical failed attempts all returned 401. Playbook requires 429 after 5 failures. attempts_doc upsert/locked_until check appears not to be firing. Test: test_lockout_after_5_failed.

minor.issue: Returns {ok: true} only; does not include access_token in body. Cookie is refreshed, but Bearer-only clients cannot rotate their Authorization header. Consider returning access_token like /register and /login do.
Response embeds token inside accept_url but does not return a top-level `token` field. Tests and UI must parse accept_url. Minor API ergonomic issue.

action_items: [HIGH] Fix brute-force lockout in /api/auth/login — after 5 failed attempts the locked_until check is not raising 429. Suspect timezone comparison in datetime.fromisoformat vs _now() (tz-aware) OR the upsert of locked_until is silently failing. Add a unit test and log the attempts_doc read before the check.
[MINOR] Consider returning access_token in /api/auth/refresh response body for bearer-only clients.
[MINOR] Add `token` field (or rename) in POST /invitations response for easier client consumption.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1592 lines — close to the 700-line recommended cap. Should be split into routers/ (auth, contexts, documents, signals, ask, audit) modules.

/api/auth/login lockout logic resets count to 0 when setting locked_until but does not also re-check attempts_doc.locked_until atomically — a small race, and combined with the bug above it silently fails open.
Refresh endpoint does not rotate the refresh token (only sets new access cookie). Consider refresh-token rotation for better security.
All GET endpoints correctly exclude _id via projection (verified in tests — check_no_mongo_id passed on every response).

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout bug: code at server.py:423-436 reads attempts_doc, checks locked_until, otherwise falls through to bcrypt check, then upserts count. After 5 fails it sets locked_until and resets count to 0. Empirical test via curl (6 identical bad-credential POSTs for a random email) returned 401 on EVERY attempt, never 429. Hypothesis: either (a) tz-aware comparison of fromisoformat(locked_until iso string with +00:00) vs _now() silently fails, or (b) the upsert of locked_until is never persisted (e.g. a missing await, or a different collection name). Reproduction: `for i in 1..6; curl -s -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} -X POST $URL/api/auth/login -d '{"email":"rnd@x.com","password":"bad"}'`. Mitigation: Add logging inside login() that prints attempts_doc after find_one and the computed count; also assert that update_one result.modified_count>=1 or upserted_id is set. Consider using a simple counter collection keyed only by email (not ip:email) for the public preview environment where client IP behind ingress is constant.
